subject: How to control digits in unmarked model summary

messages.author: d640f02d29e7de63
messages.subject: How to control digits in unmarked model summary
parts:
Dear friends,

When I summarize a model by typing its name into the console, or by typing summary(modelname), the models's estimates, SEs and their z-scores are printed with a sensible number of digits (usually four) but the P values have a ridiculous number of decimals (dozens to hundreds of digits). And the digits argument of summary() doesn't seem to control the number of digits in P values.

Can anyone help, please? I would like to truncate or round the P values to 3 or 4 digits.

Thank you,

Mark B

messages.author: d640f02d29e7de63
messages.subject: Re: How to control digits in unmarked model summary
parts: I partly solved this problem by realizing that I had previously disabled scientific notation by setting options(scipen=999). So, by setting options(scipen=3) I am able to reduce the ridiculous number of decimals but now my P values are printed in scientific notation (with 3 decimal places). What I would actually like is to print the P values in regular (not scientific) notation but to round or truncate them to 3 or 4 decimals. I understand that in some cases this will result in 0.000 and I'm fine with that. Any help much appreciated, thank you.

messages.author: 70621566ba652451
messages.subject: Re: How to control digits in unmarked model summary
parts: Maybe I am missing something, but can't you just use the round() function? I use it all the time to accomplish what you are describing. Just use the 'digits' argument to specify the number of digits past the decimal that you want, e.g., 'round(0.0052366532452346,digits=3)' will return '0.005'.
